LESSON: READING 11.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to relate what you read to real life experiences?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. create mental images from the events, characters or places in a text
2. answer direct and inferential questions from varied texts correctly

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 11.2.1 INTENSIVE READING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 11.2.1 INTENSIVE READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Create mental images from the events, characters or places in a text

What this means
In this part you learn to create mental images from the events, characters or places in a text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create mental images from the events, characters or places in a text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create mental images from the events, characters or places in a text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Answer direct and inferential questions from varied texts correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to answer direct and inferential questions from varied texts correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: answer direct and inferential questions from varied texts correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can answer direct and inferential questions from varied texts correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: create mental images from the events, characters or places in a text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading to a partner. (skill: answer direct and inferential questions from varied texts correctly)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: create mental images from the events, characters or places in a text.
3. Practise this skill: answer direct and inferential questions from varied texts correctly.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to relate what you read to real life experiences?
2. What digital resources can you use in your reading?
3. Why are digital materials more interesting to read than print ones?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: create mental images from the events, characters or places in a text.
5. Be able to: answer direct and inferential questions from varied texts correctly.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
